title: Summarize Group Discussion: tiga suara, satu ringkasan dua menit
title_target: Summarize Group Discussion — who said what, why, and what they agreed
goal: Merangkum diskusi tiga orang dalam dua menit: mencatat sikap dan alasan tiap penutur secara terpisah, lalu melaporkannya dengan kalimat sendiri — siapa berpendapat apa, di mana mereka berbeda, dan apa yang akhirnya disepakati — tanpa memasukkan pendapatmu sendiri.
bekal: mencatat diskusi tiga orang dalam tiga kolom: sikap, alasan, dan perubahan sikap tiap penutur
melaporkan pendapat orang lain dengan kata kerja pelapor dan kata hubung kontras yang tepat
menyusun ringkasan dua menit: topik → tiap penutur → titik beda → hasil diskusi

blocks.text: Summarize Group Discussion adalah salah satu dari dua tipe soal Speaking yang baru sejak 7 Agustus 2025. Kamu mendengar **tiga orang** berdiskusi — biasanya mahasiswa atau rekan kerja yang sedang memutuskan sesuatu — sepanjang **sampai 3 menit**, diputar **sekali**. Begitu audio selesai, kamu punya **10 detik** persiapan, lalu mikrofon merekam **2 menit**. Tipe ini muncul kira-kira 2–3 kali, sesudah Answer Short Question dan sebelum Respond to a Situation, dan nilainya masuk ke dua skor: Listening dan Speaking.

Ini soal Speaking terpanjang di seluruh tes, baik audionya maupun jawabanmu. **Oral fluency** dan **pronunciation** dinilai mesin seperti di tipe lain. **Content** ikut **ditinjau penilai manusia**, dan yang dicari berbeda dari Retell Lecture. Kuliah punya satu suara dan satu alur. Diskusi punya tiga suara yang saling menanggapi: ada yang setuju, ada yang membantah, ada yang menengahi, dan sering ada yang berubah pikiran. Tugasmu melaporkan **peta pendapat itu**, bukan sekadar topiknya.

head: Yang dihargai
Yang dihukum
rows: topik atau pertanyaan yang sedang diputuskan, disebut di kalimat pertama
pembuka hafalan: *The speakers discussed an interesting topic with many ideas*
sikap TIAP penutur, masing-masing dengan satu alasannya
pendapat yang dilekatkan ke orang yang salah, atau ketiga suara dilebur jadi *they said*
hubungan antar-penutur: siapa membantah siapa, siapa menengahi
daftar kata lepas: *they mentioned cost, they mentioned stress*
hasil akhir: apa yang disepakati dan apa yang masih terbuka
pendapatmu sendiri: *I think the second speaker is right*

blocks.title: Tiga hal teknis
items: **Audio hanya sekali.** Tidak ada tombol ulang, dan sesudah *Next* soal tidak bisa dibuka lagi. Tiga menit itu panjang; tanpa catatan, yang tersisa di kepalamu hanya penutur terakhir.
**Diam 3 detik = selesai.** Mikrofon berhenti merekam, status berubah jadi *Completed*, dan tidak bisa diulang. Dalam jawaban dua menit, risiko ini jauh lebih besar daripada di soal 40 detik.
**Dua menit tidak wajib diisi penuh.** Ringkasan yang rapi biasanya selesai dalam 80–110 detik. Berhenti sesudah kalimat penutup lebih aman daripada mengulang poin demi menghabiskan waktu.

blocks.text: Kesalahan paling mahal di tipe ini bukan lupa isi, melainkan **tertukar orang**. Karena itu catatanmu harus memisahkan penutur sejak detik pertama. Sebelum audio mulai, bagi papan catatan menjadi **tiga kolom**. Begitu suara pertama terdengar, beri kolom itu kode: nama kalau disebut, atau ciri suara kalau tidak.

items: **Kode penutur dulu, isi kemudian.** *A*, *B*, *C*, atau *W1* (perempuan pertama), *M* (laki-laki), *W2*. Para penutur sering saling menyapa dengan nama di kalimat-kalimat awal — tangkap di situ.
**Baris pertama tiap kolom = sikap.** Tulis *+* (mendukung), *–* (menolak), atau *±* (menengahi). Tiga simbol ini sudah separuh ringkasanmu.
**Di bawahnya, satu alasan per baris.** Dua–tiga kata: *trial: output same, stress ↓*. Jangan mengejar kalimat.
**Tanggapan ditulis dengan panah ke kolom yang ditanggapi.** *B → A: only offices*. Dari panah inilah kamu tahu siapa membantah siapa.
**Garis bawah untuk hasil.** Dua–tiga giliran terakhir hampir selalu berisi kesepakatan atau pembagian tugas. Tulis di bawah ketiga kolom dan beri tanda !

blocks.text: Di tes, nama penutur belum tentu kamu tangkap. Itu bukan masalah: *the first speaker*, *the second speaker*, *the man*, *the woman who spoke last* sama sahnya dengan nama, asal kamu **konsisten** dari awal sampai akhir jawaban.
Penanda sikap: frasa yang memberitahu arah pendapat

head: Yang kamu dengar
Artinya
Yang kamu catat
rows: *I think… · I'd say… · I'll be honest,…*
*I'm not convinced… · I'm not so sure… · But look at…*
– dan panah ke kolom yang dibantah
*That's a fair point. · True, … · I'd accept that.*
*What if we… · Can I suggest… · So maybe…*
*I still doubt… · I'm still not sure…*
*Shall we say… · So we agree that… · Then I'll…*

blocks.text: Perhatikan dua baris yang sering terlewat: **setuju dengan syarat** dan **keberatan yang tidak selesai**. Diskusi di tes jarang berakhir dengan semua orang sepakat penuh. Ringkasan yang menulis *they all agreed* padahal satu orang masih ragu adalah ringkasan yang salah isi.

sections.title: Contoh dibedah: dari diskusi ke catatan ke ringkasan

blocks.text: Diskusi di tes jauh lebih panjang, tetapi polanya sama dengan cuplikan pendek ini. Baca **satu kali** dengan kecepatan orang bicara sambil mencatat dalam tiga kolom, lalu bandingkan dengan contoh di bawahnya.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I think every lecture should be recorded and put online. If you're ill, or you miss a point, you can simply watch it again.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: I'm not so sure. When recordings are available, a lot of students stop coming, and then nobody asks questions. You lose the discussion.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Both of those are true, I think. Recordings are really useful for revision, especially for students whose first language isn't English. But they shouldn't replace attendance.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: So what would you do?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Release the recording a week later. People still have a reason to come, and it's there before the exam.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: I could accept that.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, that sounds like a reasonable compromise.

head: Ben
Chloe
Anna
rows: students stop coming → no questions, no discussion
useful revision, esp non-native · BUT not replace attendance
! agreed: record, release a week later

blocks.text: 10 detik persiapan: tentukan urutan, bukan kalimat

Sepuluh detik tidak cukup untuk menyusun kalimat. Pakai untuk satu hal: **menomori urutan bicaramu** di atas catatan — topik, lalu kolom mana dulu, lalu baris bertanda !. Urutan yang paling aman adalah urutan diskusinya sendiri, karena tanggapan baru masuk akal sesudah pendapat yang ditanggapi.

blocks.title: Model ringkasan cuplikan (83 kata)
items: The discussion was about whether lectures should be recorded. Ben was in favour, because students who are ill or miss a point can watch the lecture again. Chloe disagreed. She argued that attendance falls when recordings are available, so there is less discussion in class. Anna took a middle position: recordings help with revision, especially for non-native speakers, but they should not replace attendance. She suggested releasing each recording a week later, and in the end both Ben and Chloe accepted this compromise.

head: Yang diucapkan
Yang dilaporkan
Tekniknya
rows: *I think every lecture should be recorded*
*I'm not so sure… a lot of students stop coming*
*Chloe disagreed. She argued that attendance falls*
kata kerja pelapor + kata benda (*attendance*) menggantikan klausa
*Both of those are true, I think*
fungsi ucapan disebut, kata-katanya tidak disalin
*I could accept that. · a reasonable compromise*
*both Ben and Chloe accepted this compromise*
dua giliran digabung jadi satu kalimat hasil

blocks.text: Perhatikan yang **tidak** ada di model itu: *I*, *in my opinion*, dan penilaian tentang diskusinya. Kamu pelapor, bukan peserta keempat.

sections.title: Kerangka dua menit — dan bahasa untuk melaporkan

blocks.title: Lima langkah
items: **1. Topik (± 10 detik)** — *The discussion was about whether…* Hampir semua diskusi di tes memutuskan sesuatu, jadi *whether* + pertanyaannya adalah pembuka yang paling tepat.
**2. Penutur pertama (± 20 detik)** — sikapnya, lalu satu–dua alasan: *Anna was in favour. She pointed out that…*
**3. Penutur kedua, dihubungkan ke yang pertama (± 25 detik)** — *Ben, however, argued that…* Kata hubung kontrasnya wajib; di situlah hubungan antar-penutur terlihat.
**4. Penutur ketiga dan pergeseran (± 30 detik)** — jalan tengah, syarat, atau pembedaan yang ia tawarkan, dan bagaimana dua penutur lain menanggapinya.
**5. Hasil (± 15 detik)** — *In the end, they agreed that…* ditambah, kalau ada, satu hal yang belum selesai: *but they left… as an open question.* Lalu berhenti.

blocks.text: Urutan ini yang dihafal; kalimatnya lahir dari catatan. Kalau penutur ketiga ternyata bukan penengah melainkan pendukung salah satu pihak, langkah 4 berubah jadi *Chloe shared Ben's concern and added that…* — kerangka mengikuti diskusinya, bukan sebaliknya.

head: Fungsi
Bahasa pelapor
rows: *The discussion was about whether… · The three speakers discussed how to…*
*was in favour of… · supported the idea of… · believed that…*
*disagreed · was sceptical about… · doubted that… · raised a concern about…*
*argued that… · pointed out that… · explained that… · noted that…*
*however · whereas · while · in contrast · on the other hand*
*accepted that… · admitted that… · agreed with her on…*
*accepted this provided that… · agreed as long as…*
*In the end, they agreed that… · They decided to… · They left… as an open question.*

blocks.text: Pakai **past tense** untuk melaporkan apa yang dikatakan (*Ben argued*) dan **present tense** untuk isi pendapat yang berlaku umum (*museums are expensive to run*). Variasikan kata kerja pelapornya: lima kali *said* berturut-turut terdengar seperti daftar.

head: Yang sering terdengar
Masalahnya
Yang seharusnya
rows: *dia* tidak membedakan jenis kelamin; dalam laporan tiga orang, *he* dan *she* yang tertukar membuat pendapat pindah pemilik
pakai nama atau *the first speaker* kalau ragu
*Ben is agree with Anna.* · *Chloe is disagree.*
*They discussed museums.* · *The discussion was about museums.*
dobel pelapor, terjemahan *menurut Ben, dia bilang*
*According to Ben, museums need income.* atau *Ben said that…*
tanpa akhiran lampau, dan *suggest to* tidak baku
pendapat pribadi tidak diminta dan tidak dinilai

blocks.title: Kalau kamu ketinggalan
items: **Tidak yakin siapa yang mengatakan sesuatu?** Laporkan tanpa pemilik: *One speaker pointed out that…* Itu jujur dan tetap bernilai. Menempelkannya ke orang yang salah lebih merugikan.

**Kehilangan satu penutur?** Laporkan dua yang kamu tangkap dengan alasan masing-masing, lalu hasilnya. Jangan mengarang pendapat untuk yang ketiga: penilai manusia membandingkan jawabanmu dengan isi diskusinya.
**Tidak menangkap kesepakatannya?** Tutup dengan apa yang pasti: *The speakers did not fully agree, but they shared the view that…*
**Buntu saat bicara?** Jangan diam dan jangan meralat. Lompat ke kolom berikutnya di catatan. Dua menit terasa lama, tetapi tiga detik diam tetap menutup mikrofon.
**Selesai di detik ke-80?** Berhenti. Mengulang poin atau menambah opini merusak fluency dan tidak menambah content.

blocks.text: Putar audionya dulu dan kerjakan latihan TANPA membaca naskah di bawah; naskah ini untuk memeriksa sesudahnya.

Urutan kerja: dengarkan Discussion 1 **sekali** sambil mencatat tiga kolom → hentikan audio, hitung 10 detik → rekam ringkasanmu 2 menit di ponsel. Ulangi untuk Discussion 2. **Hentikan audio sebelum bagian *Model answer*** — itu model ringkasan Discussion 1 yang dibacakan, untuk didengar sesudah kedua rekamanmu selesai.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: OK, so for the seminar we have to decide whether companies should move to a four-day working week. I'll be honest, I think the answer is yes. In the big trial in Britain a couple of years ago, most of the companies that took part decided to keep the shorter week afterwards. Output stayed about the same, and staff reported much less stress and took fewer sick days.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I've read about that trial, Anna, but look at who took part. They were mostly offices: marketing firms, software companies, charities. I'm not convinced it works in a hospital, a shop or a factory. If nurses work four days instead of five, the patients are still there on the fifth day, so the hospital has to employ more people. That's a real cost, and someone has to pay for it.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: I think you're talking about two different things, though. There are really two models. In one, people work fewer hours for the same pay, about thirty-two a week. In the other, they squeeze the same forty hours into four long days. The trial Anna mentioned used the first model. The second one is cheaper for employers, but ten-hour days can leave people more tired, not less.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: That's a fair point. I'd only defend the first model. A compressed week isn't really a shorter week at all.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Fine, but then my objection is even stronger. Fewer hours for the same pay only works if people get more done per hour. In an office you can cut long meetings and wasted time. A bus driver can't drive the route any faster.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: So maybe our argument shouldn't be that every company should do it. What if we say it suits work where output isn't tied to the hours you're physically present, and that other sectors need a different solution, like more flexible shifts?

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: I can live with that, as long as we still say the evidence for office work is strong. And we could recommend that companies run a six-month pilot and measure the results before they decide.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, a pilot makes sense. I'd support that. I'll look for figures on staffing costs in healthcare, so we can show where the limits are.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: Great. Then Anna covers the trial results, Ben covers the limits, and I'll explain the two models at the start.

blocks.title: Discussion 2: Should museums charge for entry?

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: Our topic is whether public museums should charge for entry, and I'd say they shouldn't. These collections are paid for by taxpayers, so in a sense they already belong to everyone. A ticket price keeps out exactly the people who can least afford it, like students and families on low incomes. When the national museums in Britain dropped their charges in 2001, visitor numbers rose sharply.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: They did, Chloe, but numbers aren't the whole story. Some research suggests that many of those extra visits were made by people who already went to museums, and by tourists. Meanwhile, museums are expensive to run. Old objects have to be conserved, buildings need repairs, and expert staff have to be paid. If government funding is cut, a museum with no ticket income has nothing to fall back on.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Can I suggest something in between? Plenty of museums keep the permanent collection free but sell tickets for special exhibitions. That way nobody is shut out of the main galleries, and the people who want to see something extra help to pay for it.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: I'd accept that, provided there are cheaper tickets for students and children. Otherwise the most exciting exhibitions become something only wealthier visitors see.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I'm fine with discounts. But I still doubt it raises enough. Special exhibitions cost a lot to put on, so the profit can be small.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: True, which is why I'd add donations. Some museums put a box by the entrance with a suggested amount, and more and more let you pay by card. Visitors who can afford it often give something.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Often, but not reliably. You can't plan a budget around a donation box. I'd rather see a small compulsory charge for overseas tourists, who haven't paid for the museum through their taxes.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: Hmm, that seems hard to enforce. Would staff check passports at the door? I'm not sure that's the welcome a museum wants to give.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: We don't have to settle that today. Shall we say we agree on the main point: general admission stays free, special exhibitions are ticketed with discounts, and donations are encouraged?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Agreed, as long as we note that I think donations alone won't be enough.

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: That's fair. We'll present the tourist charge as an open question rather than a recommendation.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: The discussion was about whether companies should adopt a four-day working week. Anna was clearly in favour. She pointed out that in a large British trial most companies kept the shorter week, because output stayed about the same while stress and sick days fell.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: Ben was more sceptical. He argued that the trial mainly involved offices, and that in hospitals, shops or factories the work still has to be done on the fifth day, so employers would need extra staff, which costs money.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: Chloe then made a distinction between two models: working fewer hours for the same pay, and squeezing forty hours into four long days, which is cheaper but more tiring. Anna agreed that only the first model is worth defending, whereas Ben replied that it only works where people can get more done per hour.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: In the end, the three speakers reached a compromise. They decided to argue that a four-day week suits jobs where output does not depend on hours of presence, while other sectors need solutions such as flexible shifts. They also agreed to recommend a six-month pilot before any decision is made.

sections.title: Tugas rekam dan cara menilai diri

blocks.title: Tugas — dua ringkasan, masing-masing 2 menit
items: Kerjakan seperti di tes: audio sekali, 10 detik, lalu rekam dengan timer. Jangan menjeda audio di tengah diskusi dan jangan menulis kalimat utuh di catatan.
Sesudah kedua rekaman selesai, kerjakan Latihan dari **catatanmu**, bukan dari naskah. Baru sesudah itu dengarkan *Model answer* Discussion 1 di audio dan baca model Discussion 2 di *Pembahasan*.

blocks.title: Daftar periksa
items: **Topik** — apakah kalimat pertamamu memuat pertanyaan yang sedang diputuskan (*whether…*), bukan hanya bidangnya?
**Tiga suara** — apakah ketiga penutur muncul, masing-masing dengan sikap dan minimal satu alasan? Cocokkan dengan naskah: adakah pendapat yang salah pemilik?
**Hubungan** — tandai setiap *however, whereas, agreed, accepted, replied*. Kalau tidak ada, jawabanmu masih tiga ringkasan terpisah, bukan ringkasan sebuah diskusi.
**Hasil** — apakah kamu menyebut apa yang disepakati DAN apa yang masih terbuka atau bersyarat?
**Netral** — adakah *I think* atau *in my opinion*? Hapus.
**Irama** — jeda panjang, pengulangan, ralat: targetnya nol. Catat detik selesaimu; 80–110 detik adalah rentang yang sehat.

blocks.text: Kalau rekaman pertamamu berhenti di detik ke-50, biasanya alasan tiap penutur terlewat dan kamu hanya menyebut sikapnya. Kalau kamu terpotong di detik ke-120, biasanya kamu menceritakan ulang giliran demi giliran, bukan merangkum per penutur. Untuk skor mesin yang sebenarnya, pakai tes latihan resmi berskor dari Pearson; di kelas Private PTE Linguo, catatan dan rekamanmu dibedah bersama pengajar.

(B) Invent a detailed argument for the third speaker so that all three get equal time. (C) Repeat the first speaker's view three times in different words to fill the two minutes. ____

answers: Anna — Chloe — Ben — Chloe — Anna — Ben
in favour of — pointed — proposed — provided that — In the end

head: No
Jawaban
Alasan & pengecoh
rows: Chloe: *it suits work where output isn't tied to the hours you're physically present*; Anna menambah *a six-month pilot*, dan Ben: *a pilot makes sense*. (A) sikap awal Anna yang kemudian dilunakkan — Chloe: *our argument shouldn't be that every company should do it*; (C) model kedua justru dikritik (*more tired, not less*) dan tidak dibela siapa pun; (D) Ben menyebut biaya, tetapi tidak ada yang menolak gagasannya secara keseluruhan.

*look at who took part. They were mostly offices*. (A) bertentangan: *most… decided to keep the shorter week*; (B) bertentangan: *much less stress*; (C) masuk akal di dunia nyata, tetapi lamanya uji coba tidak dipersoalkan.

*keep the permanent collection free but sell tickets for special exhibitions*. (B) tidak diusulkan siapa pun — diskon pelajar adalah syarat Chloe untuk pameran khusus, bukan tiket umum; (C) tidak disebut; (D) itu usul Ben, bukan Anna.

Chloe: *We'll present the tourist charge as an open question rather than a recommendation*. (A) sudah selesai — Ben: *I'm fine with discounts*; (B) justru itu yang disepakati: *general admission stays free*; (D) pembayaran dengan kartu hanya disebut sekilas oleh Anna, tidak diperdebatkan.
Giliran pembukanya: *Output stayed about the same, and staff reported much less stress*. Ben hanya berkata ia sudah membaca tentang uji coba itu, lalu mempersoalkan pesertanya.
*I think you're talking about two different things… There are really two models*. Anna baru menanggapi sesudahnya (*I'd only defend the first model*).
*A bus driver can't drive the route any faster* — contoh untuk keberatannya bahwa jam lebih pendek hanya berhasil kalau hasil per jam bisa naik.
*A ticket price keeps out exactly the people who can least afford it, like students and families on low incomes*.
*which is why I'd add donations. Some museums put a box by the entrance*. Ben menanggapi usul ini, bukan mengajukannya.
*You can't plan a budget around a donation box*. Kata *donation* muncul di giliran Anna dan Ben; yang membedakan adalah sikapnya — Anna mengusulkan, Ben meragukan.
*was in favour of* + kata benda. Sikap Chloe sejak kalimat pertama: *I'd say they shouldn't* (memungut tiket).
*pointed out that…* — satu-satunya kata di kotak yang berpasangan dengan *out*. *denied* berarti menyangkal, dan Ben justru mengakui angka kunjungan naik (*They did*).
*proposed a compromise*. Anna membuka dengan *Can I suggest something in between?* — *denied a compromise* berlawanan artinya.
Chloe: *I'd accept that, provided there are cheaper tickets for students and children*. Ini setuju bersyarat; menghilangkan syaratnya mengubah isi.
Penanda hasil. *according to* harus diikuti sumber (*according to Ben*), jadi tidak bisa berdiri di depan koma.
Menyebut pertanyaan yang diputuskan dan langsung dua sikap yang berlawanan dengan *while*. (A) daftar kata lepas tanpa sikap dan tanpa hubungan; (C) pendapat pribadi — tidak ada di diskusinya.

Sesuai giliran penutup Anna dan Chloe, termasuk hal yang belum selesai. (A) kalimat hafalan yang cocok untuk diskusi apa pun; (B) salah isi: hanya Ben yang mengusulkan pungutan turis, dan Chloe menolaknya.
Dua pendapat yang benar pemiliknya ditambah hasil tetap mendapat nilai content. (B) karangan terbaca oleh penilai manusia; (C) pengulangan merusak fluency dan tidak menambah isi.

blocks.text: Model Discussion 1 ada di audio (*Model answer*, 187 kata, ± 85 detik) dan tercetak di bagian *Naskah audio latihan*. Dengarkan iramanya: jeda hanya di titik dan koma, dan tiap penutur dibuka dengan namanya.

blocks.title: Discussion 2 · Should museums charge for entry?
items: The discussion was about whether public museums should charge for entry. Chloe was in favour of free entry. She argued that the collections are funded by taxpayers and that ticket prices exclude students and low-income families, and she noted that visitor numbers rose sharply when British national museums became free in 2001. Ben, however, pointed out that many of those extra visits came from people who already went to museums, and that museums are costly to run, so they need an income if government funding is cut. Anna then proposed a compromise: keep the permanent collection free and sell tickets for special exhibitions. Chloe accepted this provided that students and children get cheaper tickets. Ben doubted that it would raise enough money, so Anna added the idea of donations, which Ben considered unreliable. He suggested a compulsory charge for overseas tourists instead, but Chloe thought it would be hard to enforce. In the end, they agreed that general admission should stay free, with ticketed special exhibitions and encouraged donations, and they left the tourist charge as an open question.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat
items: Kedua model berjalan di urutan yang sama — topik, tiap penutur dengan alasannya, pergeseran, hasil — tetapi tidak ada satu kalimat pun yang bisa dipindah ke diskusi lain. Kerangka dihafal, isi tidak.
Hitung kata kerja pelapornya: *argued, noted, pointed out, proposed, accepted, doubted, suggested, agreed*. Tiap kata membawa informasi tentang sikap; *said* tidak.

Kesepakatan di kedua diskusi **tidak bulat**: Anna setuju dengan syarat, Ben masih ragu soal donasi, pungutan turis dibiarkan terbuka. Melaporkan sisa perbedaan itu adalah bagian dari content, bukan detail tambahan.
